chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When they see the crescent before the decline (of the sun), it is for the past night, and when they see it after the decline, it is for the coming night.
ai.seo_question: How is the start of a lunar month determined based on crescent sighting time in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential principle that the visibility of the crescent is determined by its appearance relative to solar noon (Zawal), a key criterion in Shia lunar calendar calculations. It establishes that a pre-noon sighting validates the preceding night, while a post-noon sighting initiates the upcoming night, ensuring precise alignment of religious observances like Ramadan with astronomical reality.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you see the crescent before the decline (of the sun), so it is its past night, and when you see it after the decline (of the sun), so it is its coming night’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If they can see the crescent before Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime), then it is of the last night but if they see it after Zawal, then it is of the coming night.’”
